# backup-gate

> Free, open-source macOS tool (MIT) that keeps malware out of Time Machine backups. Time Machine backs up only when nothing that can run code at startup has changed since the user approved it. When a launch agent, login item, shell startup file, sudoers rule or similar changes, the backup waits until the user reviews and approves the change. Without it, malware that installs itself is copied into every backup and comes back on restore or Migration Assistant, while the clean backups from before the infection age out of Time Machine's limited history.

- One bash script (about 550 lines) plus a LaunchDaemon; no dependencies, no network access.
- Requires a local Time Machine disk (USB/Thunderbolt APFS); network/NAS destinations aren't supported.
- Install: `brew install mermoddity/backup-gate/backup-gate` (Apple silicon), then `sudo $(brew --prefix)/opt/backup-gate/libexec/install.sh`; or from a GitHub release with SHA-256 and build attestation.
- Doesn't remove malware; malware with root can disable it; doesn't detect ransomware changing documents.
- Complements Objective-See's BlockBlock (real-time persistence alerts) and KnockKnock (persistence scan).
